  • downward closer to the valence band, away from the middle of the forbidden

  • and second-order polarization such that 𝐸→−𝐸 and 𝑃(2)→−𝑃(2). (1 Mark)
  • Substituting this into the nonlinear relation gives −𝑃(2)=𝑃(2), which forces
  • 𝑃(2)=0 and consequently 𝜒(2)=0, prohibiting second-harmonic generation.

questions.question: How is photosensitivity at ~240nm utilized to fabricate periodic gratings in germanium-doped silica fibres? / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• How is photosensitivity at ~240nm utilized to fabricate periodic gratings in
  • germanium-doped silica fibres?

  • induced in germanium doped silica by forming an interference pattern within
  • the fibre core from two coherent UV laser light beams incident at an angle to the
  • fibre axis. (1 Mark)
  • The glass core of the fibre is photosensitive at ~ 240 nm and this wavelength
  • may be obtained by harmonic generation from a longer wavelength laser, or it
  • may be directly produced by a pulsed ultraviolet excimer laser. (1 Mark)

questions.question: Explain the working of a semiconductor laser with a suitable energy level diagram. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the working of a semiconductor laser with a suitable energy level
  • diagram.
  • Energy Level Diagram (2 Marks)
  • Basic Principle & Requirements (3 Mark)
  • The semiconductor material must have a high transition probability for
  • radiative transitions across the bandgap, exceeding non-radiative lattice
  • transfer rates. Population inversion is achieved via carrier injection through a
  • forward biasing of the semiconductor diode.
  • The 𝑝-𝑛 junction diode must be heavily doped. In the 𝑛-type region, the Fermi
  • level 𝐹𝑐 lies within the conduction band, while in the 𝑝-type region, the Fermi
  • level 𝐹𝑣 lies within the valence band.
  • When forward-biased, electrons are injected into the 𝑝-side and holes into the
  • 𝑛-side, creating a high concentration of both carriers in the narrow
  • depletion/active region. This high concentration results in a population
  • inversion between the conduction band, and the valence band states near the
  • junction. Electron-hole recombination in this narrow planar region releases
  • coherent optical radiation when the injected current exceeds a threshold value.
  • Optical Confinement & Resonator Action (1 Marks)
  • Laser action is confined to the very thin junction region.
  • The crystal end faces are cleaved parallel to form an optical resonator, providing
  • the necessary feedback for amplification and stimulated emission.
  • [U]/[CO1]

questions.question: Discuss the principle and operational mechanism of a Kerr-cell Q-switch in a laser system. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Discuss the principle and operational mechanism of a Kerr-cell Q-switch in a
  • laser system
  • Explanation of Kerr effect (1.5 Mark)
  • A Kerr cell consists of an isotropic liquid (such as nitrobenzene) containing
  • asymmetric molecules placed between parallel plates. When an external electric
  • field is applied, the molecules tend to align parallel to the field direction and the
  • liquid become optically anisotropic and birefringent, with refractive indices 𝑛𝑜
  • and 𝑛𝑒 proportional to the square of the applied voltage.
  • The Kerr Cell Shutter System-Schematic OR Explanation (1.5 Marks)
  • [U]/ [CO2]
  • Operational Sequence (2 Marks)
  • The Kerr cell is activated by applying a high bias voltage (10--20 kV).
  • The flash lamp is fired to pump the active laser medium.
  • After population inversion peaks (approx. 0.5 ms), the Kerr cell voltage is
  • switched off as suddenly as possible.
  • Performance Characteristics (1 Mark)
  • Operating as a fast electro-optic shutter, switching times in the nanosecond
  • range. Effectively increases peak output power (e.g., from kilowatts to
  • megawatts/gigawatts) by compressing the energy into a giant optical pulse.
